product_from_film: Supermemory presents a shared memory layer for multiple AI apps, with an installation command, content-source connections and a memory-informed coding request.
explains_well: The central memory diagram connects several named AI apps, making the cross-app idea easy to grasp.
unclear: The beach rescue joke never connects to a specific memory failure or repaired task, and the demo does not trace one remembered fact between two apps.
scenario: Connect memory across AI tools and bring in stored content to inform a project request.
product_clear_basis: The ASR introduces universal memory at 63.6s; the shared-memory diagram appears around 66s. Earlier talk concerns a prior MCP release.

sound.detail: The opening draft contains short distressed exclamations and garbled references to ChatGPT. It is insufficient to establish the precise skit dialogue. No voice, music, effects or sync were heard.

The usable draft discusses memory lock-in, a previous MCP release, universal memory, one-command installation, preferences and connected sources. Some app names, numerical claims and the URL are mistranscribed; visible labels take priority. All sound and the final hold remain unassessed.
sound.evidence: Local 478-speech.json plus visible cards and URL.

categories.finding: The diagram and example explain the general concept without sound; the opening skit’s intended logic is less clear.
The presenter anchors the overlays, while the standalone diagram makes app relationships easier to scan.
The new universal-memory pitch arrives after roughly a minute of skit, problem and prior traction; the final URL holds for about nine seconds.
The memory promise gets an example of project context retrieval, but no visible transfer of the same fact across apps.
The skit may attract attention and the founder framing may build familiarity; response unmeasured.
The central memory box connects the app icons; the example connects remembered project context to a schema answer.
Memory scope, cross-app behavior, privacy, installation success, usage metrics and answer correctness are unverified. Visible and ASR star counts differ, so no reconciled count is asserted.
The shared-memory diagram distinguishes the product from one assistant’s internal memory.
Trace one memory between two apps.
